reason: Conversation 2 correctly kept the diagnosis uncertain between the mains suppression filter and the control board, explicitly told the homeowner not to open the machine, covered the sensible supply checks (spur, consumer unit, dud fuse, longer reset) in one efficient pass, and pointed him to Candy/Haier service or an engineer plus the model number. Conversation 1 reached the right escalation but leaned on an 'internal fuse on the PCB' narrative, drifted toward asking him to check 'continuity in the plug/cable assembly' (an inappropriate nudge toward electrical testing), never mentioned the filter, and padded every reply with an irrelevant tripping/burning boilerplate panel. Conversation 2's only real weakness is ordering 'call your home insurer first' ahead of the warranty check, though it hedged with 'often covered' rather than asserting surge damage as certain.
